claims.head: Strength against strength
claims.body: The Lightning are near the top of the league for chance quality, and the Kraken are near the top of the league at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Kraken’s defense.
claims.call: The Kraken keep the Lightning’s chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot).
claims.nums: Tampa Bay 8th for chance quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Seattle 6th for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: It’s strength against strength: the Lightning for chance quality, the Kraken at preventing dangerous shots.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 5 games this season

check.measure: the average shot’s chance of going in, by expected goals
check.rule: held if tonight's figure lands on the predicted side of the league average; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Lightning will send McDonagh and Cernak at Eberle
claims.call: The Lightning’s P2 (McDonagh and Cernak) spends at least 51% of its 5-on-5 time against the Kraken’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending McDonagh and Cernak out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would. That’s Jon Cooper picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Kraken’s first line is Eberle, Stephenson and McMann.
claims.nums: At home: 51% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 32% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Jon Cooper likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Kraken’s first line.

check.measure: share of Tampa Bay P2's 5-on-5 time against Seattle L1
check.rule: held if the share is at or above the home habit; partly if above the no-matching level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Lightning are going to test the Kraken’s goalie early and often
claims.call: The Lightning take at least their usual 64.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: Few teams shoot like the Lightning, and the Kraken are the league’s worst at keeping shots away. It could be a long night in the Kraken’s end.
claims.nums: Tampa Bay 4th for shot volume (64.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Seattle 32nd for shot suppression
claims.gist: The Lightning shoot a lot, and the Kraken give up plenty.

notes.text: E. Lilleberg has been a scratch for the last 3 games. He is a top-four defenseman. M. Crozier has taken his spot beside C. D'Astous.

TBL.head: A big edge for Tampa Bay
TBL.body: Tampa Bay has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Seattle’s only real way in is pouncing on loose pucks, and they would need a near-perfect night.

SEA.head: Everything points away from Seattle
SEA.body: Tampa Bay has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Seattle could still pull it off if they pounce on loose pucks, but they might need a miracle.
